speech_verification.heard: The Hindenburg burned in 32 seconds, yet most people on board survived. Popular memory pictures a total loss of life. 35 individuals died among the 97 on board. Cabin boy Werner Franz escaped after a burst water tank doused him. Captain Max Pruss also survived despite severe burns. Over 60 people were rescued alive from the wreckage. Most people on board survived when it burned.

notes.hook: The opening line and on-screen text reveal the survival twist immediately, spoiling the curiosity gap.
notes.clarity: The script clearly breaks down the survival rate and provides specific examples of those who lived.
notes.payoff: Because the survival outcome is stated in the first two seconds, the ending feels repetitive rather than surprising.
notes.visuals: Excellent use of distinct archival photos to illustrate the ship, the disaster, and the setting.
notes.loop: The transition from the final word back to the start of the hook is seamless and rhythmically consistent.
notes.accuracy: The script includes an unsupported strawman about popular memory and ignores the ground crew fatality mentioned in research.
